rebuttal_or_critique: While I acknowledge the concerns of my colleagues regarding the 8.30% food inflation, I maintain that this is primarily a supply-side phenomenon that monetary policy is ill-equipped to address. With core inflation at 3.60%, the real policy rate is already significantly positive, which is sufficient to anchor expectations. Continuing the 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance when the output gap is positive at 0.50% and core inflation is well-contained risks an unnecessary tightening of financial conditions that could dampen the 6.80% GVA growth momentum. A shift to a neutral stance better reflects the current macroeconomic reality where the policy rate is already at a level that balances inflation control with growth support.
